items.stem:
Logistic Leaders is a transportation company that uses a database table SHIPMENT to store information about shipment details. Here is the table structure of SHIPMENT.
SHIPMENT
Field name
Description
SHIPID
Identity code of each shipment
ORIGIN
Name of the city where the shipment originated
DESTINATION
Name of the city where the shipment is being delivered
PICKUP_DATE
The date when the shipment was picked up from the original location
DELIVERY_DATE
The date when the shipment was delivered to the destination location. This attribute will be empty if the shipment is still in transit
STATUS
The current status of the shipment (1 means delivered, 0 means in transit)

parts.label: a
parts.text:
Complete the SQL statements below to create the database table SHIPMENT.(3 marks)
CREATE TABLE SHIPMENT (
SHIPID VARCHAR(10) ______________,
ORIGIN VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
____________________________,
PICKUP_DATE DATE NOT NULL,
____________________________,
STATUS BOOL
)

parts.label: b
parts.text:
Explain briefly how the following SQL command affects the table SHIPMENT. (1 mark)
ALTER TABLE SHIPMENT ADD MEMBERID CHAR(10)
[--Answer:
(a) CREATE TABLE SHIPMENT (
SHIPID VARCHAR(10) PRIMARY KEY,
ORIGIN VARCHAR(50)NOT NULL,
DESTINATION VARCHAR(50)NOT NULL,
PICKUP_DATE DATE NOT NULL,
DELIVERY_DATE DATE,
STATUS BOOL
)
(b) It adds a new column called MEMBERID to the SHIPMENT table with a data type of CHAR(10).
--]

Mr Chau operates a restaurant and uses a database table MENU to store the information on the menu item so that customers can view the menu on their website.
Some of the data stored in the mentioned table is shown below.
MENUID
NAME
PRICE
PREPTIME
01
Margherita Pizza
101
25
02
Caesar Salad
65
10
03
Spaghetti and Meatballs
89
20

parts.label: a
parts.text:
Mr Chau wants to add a new feature to the website that allows customers to order food for delivery. To implement this feature, the restaurant needs to store whether the food is available for delivery.
Here is the new table structure of MENU.
Field name
Description
MENUID
Identity code of each menu item
NAME
The name of the menu item
PRICE
The price of the menu item
PREPTIME
The estimated time (in minutes) required to prepare the menu item
DELIVERY
Whether the item can be delivered (1 means yes; 0 means no)
Write a SQL command to add a new field DELIVERY to table MENU.  (2 marks)

parts.label: b
parts.text:
Mr Chau decides to set a constraint to ensure that the preparation time for all menu items is at most 30 minutes. Write a SQL command to commit his change.  (2 marks)
[--Answer:
(a) ALTER TABLE MENU ADD DELIVERY BOOL
(b) ALTER TABLE MENU
ADD CONSTRAINT CHECK (PREPTIME <= 30)
--]

Here are some data of SONGS.
TITLE
ARTIST
ALBUM
RELEASE
RATING
Hey Jude
The Beatles

1970-02-26
5

Queen

1975-10-31
3

parts.label: a
parts.text:
SONGS is created by the SQL statement below.
CREATE TABLE SONGS (
TITLE VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
ARTIST VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
ALBUM VARCHAR(255),
RELEASE DATE,
RATING INT DEFAULT 0,
)
Can we set TITLE as the primary key of SONGS? Explain briefly.  (2 marks)

parts.label: b
parts.text:
Write a SQL statement that can generate the following result.  (3 marks)
Result
Billie Jean
Michael Jackson
Stairway to Heaven
Led Zeppelin
[--Answer:
(a) A primary key is a unique identifier for each row in a table. However, two songs could have the same title. In this case, storing both songs in the table with TITLE as the primary key would be impossible. Thus, we cannot set TITLE as the primary key of SONGS.
(b) SELECT TITLE, ARTIST
FROM SONGS
WHERE RATING = 4
ORDER BY RELEASE DESC
Or any reasonable answers.
--]

items.stem:
Harry developed a game and used database tables LEVELS to store information on different levels of players and LEADERBOARD to store players’ scores and rankings. Players’ progress has been tracked through the levels and allowed to resume their progress later.
LEVELS
Field name
Description
LEVEL
The level number
NAME
The name of each level
DIFFICULTY
The difficulty level of each level
SCORE
The score value for each level
Primary key: LEVEL
LEADERBOARD
Field name
Description
RANK
Rank according to players’ score
PLAYER
The name of each player
LEVEL
The level number that players achieve
TOTALSCORE
The sum of the player's scores across all levels
Primary key: RANK

parts.label: a
parts.text:
Harry accidentally decreased the scores of all levels with an Easy difficulty by 100 points, so now he wishes to change this back.
Write an SQL command to add the score to the corresponding player’s account.  (2 marks)

parts.label: b
parts.text:
Harry has merged the LEADERBOARD table with a new table, and he needs to delete the LEADERBOARD table now. Which approach would be more appropriate for Harry to delete the table? (2 marks)
DELETE FROM LEADERBOARD
DROP TABLE LEADERBOARD
[--Answer:
(a) UPDATE LEVELS
SET SCORE = SCORE + 100
WHERE DIFFICULTY = 'Easy'
(b) As the DROP command deletes an entire table, while the DELETE command will only remove records in the LEADERBOARD table. Thus, in this case, DROP TABLE LEADERBOARD is more appropriate.
--]

parts.label: a

DOCTOR CHAR(4) NOT NULL,

)

parts.label: ii
parts.text: Write a SQL command to list the appointment date of patient P02083. The latest appointments will be shown first. (2 marks)

parts.label: d
parts.text:
The hospital is now using a new table to store all staff working in the hospital instead of categorising the job like the DOCTOR table. Write a SQL command to drop the DOCTOR table.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write a SQL to list all available rooms with their ROOMID, TYPE, and PRICE. (2 marks)

parts.label: i
parts.text:
Room number 610 is currently undergoing renovation and is not available for booking. An employee wishes to remove this record from the ROOMS table and thus executes the following SQL command.
DELETE FROM ROOM WHERE ROOMID = 610
Explain briefly why the following SQL statement cannot be executed. (2 marks)

parts.label: ii
parts.text: Write a SQL statement that should be executed before removing ROOMID 610 from the ROOMS table. (2 marks)

parts.label: c
parts.text:
Guest G01 checked in on 2023-07-14 and would like to check out later. Update his reservation to change the check-out date to '2023-07-23'. (2 marks)
[--Answer:
(a) SELECT ROOMID, TYPE, PRICE
FROM ROOMS
WHERE AVAILABILITY = 'A'

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(i) As the ROOMS table has a foreign key ROOMID with the RESERVATIONS table, if there are any reservations made for room 610, deleting the record from the ROOMS table will violate the foreign key constraint.
(ii) DELETE FROM RESERVATIONS
WHERE ROOMID = 610
(c) UPDATE RESERVATIONS
SET CHKOUT = '2023-07-23'
WHERE GUESTID = 'G01' AND CHKIN = '2023-07-14'
--]
